}}'''Guy Roderick Wilkinson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 1968 at Ashton-under-Lyne)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Wilkinson, Prof. Guy Roderick | id = .U291026 | year = 2019 | doi = | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is an English [[particle physicist]], working on the [[Large Hadron Collider]] project at [[CERN]],<ref name=frs/> professor of physics at the [[University of Oxford]] and a [[Fellow]] of [[Christ Church, Oxford|Christ Church]], where he holds the college's Alfred Moritz [[Studentship#United Kingdom|Studentship]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chch.ox.ac.uk/staff/professor-guy-wilkinson |website=Christ Church |access-date=18 January 2021|title=Professor Guy Wilkinson FRS &#124; Christ Church, Oxford University }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/wilkinsong|title=Guy Wilkinson - University of Oxford Department of Physics|website=physics.ox.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Education==
Wilkinson was educated at [[Bishop's Stortford College]],<ref name=whoswho/> [[Imperial College London]]<ref name=chch/> and the [[University of Oxford]] where he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] degree at [[Magdalen College, Oxford|Magdalen College]] in 1993 for a study of B⁰B⁰ oscillations at the Z⁰ resonance.<ref name=glwdphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015949338|title=A study of B⁰ B⁰ oscillations at the Z⁰ resonance|first= Guy R.|last=Wilkinson|date=1993|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.334888}}|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk|oclc=83037077}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Wilkinson's career began in the study of electroweak physics on the [[DELPHI experiment]], taking part in the measurement of the mass and width of the Z boson, and the mass of the W boson. Wilkinson currently specialises in [[CP-violation]] through measurements of processes involving the decays of [[hadron]]s containing beauty or charm quarks. He is a founding member and former spokesperson of the [[LHCb]] experiment on the Large Hadron Collider at CERN.

===Awards and honours===
In 2017, he was awarded the [[James Chadwick Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]] (IOP) for his work on heavy quarks.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/guy-wilkinson-13852/|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|title=Professor Guy Wilkinson FRS|year=2018}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref><ref name=chch>{{cite web|url=https://www.chch.ox.ac.uk/staff/professor-guy-wilkinson|title=Professor Guy Wilkinson - Christ Church, Oxford University|website=chch.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/new-subatomic-particle-large-hadron-collider-baryon-quark-heavier-than-proton-a7828621.html|title=Scientists have discovered an entirely new type of particle|publisher=[[The Independent]]|website=independent.co.uk|date=2017-07-07}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2018.<ref name=frs/>
